name: Aluf Plastics
old_description: As a global manufacturer of compostable sealant, barrier sealant films, and laminates, we serve a diverse range of industries including food, beverage, medical, personal care, office, industrial, and other consumer packaged goods (CPG) segments.
about:
Earthfirst Films, a division of Aluf Plastics, is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, with additional manufacturing sites in Orangeburg, New York, and Sulphur Springs, Texas. The business traces its roots to 1949 when Joe Tatem founded Plastic Suppliers as a privately held corporation in Blackwood, New Jersey. Over decades the company expanded through distribution centers and converting facilities across the United States and Europe, eventually establishing film manufacturing in Columbus in 1974. In 2025 the Earthfirst Films brand was acquired by API, continuing its focus on sustainable packaging.

The company manufactures compostable sealant films, barrier sealant films, and laminates using blown film extrusion and cast-and-tenter extrusion technologies. Its Columbus campus operates a blown film facility at 2450 Marilyn Lane and a tenter film facility at 2400 Marilyn Lane, supported by an on-site laboratory equipped with two lab extruders for tensile, barrier, FTIR, and microscopy testing. Capabilities include lamination, high-speed slitting, converting, and fast prototyping with small-batch production runs.

Earthfirst Films serves the food, beverage, medical, personal care, office, industrial, and broader consumer packaged goods (CPG) sectors. Its films are used in applications such as flow wrap, shrink sleeve decoration, and print web structures, targeting brands that require certified home-compostable or industrial-compostable packaging solutions.

The company states its mission is to create sustainable solutions through open collaboration. It highlights a legacy of over 20 years in biopolymer film extrusion, holding several patents on compostable sealant films, and offering materials beyond PLA, including PHA and other biobased polymers. The 2019 SQF certification for its blown film facility underscores a commitment to food-grade packaging standards.
